br01.gold_connection: Refund requests clustering within two days of a promo launch, on orders paid with newly added cards, are stolen-card validation runs, so the refund queue is the earliest fraud signal the store has.
br01.gold_implication: Pull refunds requested within 48 hours of each promo launch, filter to payment methods under 7 days old, and check how many of those orders became chargebacks 30 to 60 days later.
br01.hidden_mechanism: refund clusters right after promo launches are stolen-card validation runs

br02.gold_connection: One delivery address receiving orders under many different customer names is a reshipping drop point for goods bought with stolen cards, the same pattern the processor flags as freight-forwarder addresses.
br02.gold_implication: Count distinct customer names per shipping address over the last 90 days and hold any address above five for manual review before dispatch.
br02.hidden_mechanism: many customer names shipping to one address is a reshipping drop point for stolen-card goods

br04.gold_connection: Evaluators weight the first-listed criterion most, so the order of a rubric changes the ranking: grant panels write most about the first section and LLM judges spread scores widest on the first criterion.
br04.gold_implication: Score the same ten outputs with the rubric criteria in two different orders and compare which outputs rank top under each.
br04.hidden_mechanism: the criterion listed first gets the most weight from evaluators

br05.gold_connection: A schedule set relative to the previous event drifts later every cycle and falls out of a fixed window, whether the window is a gateway's wake slot or a morning injection hour.
br05.gold_implication: Set the dose reminder to a fixed clock time for two weeks and count doses inside the window against the previous two weeks.
br05.hidden_mechanism: a fixed receiving window fails when the sending schedule is relative to the last event and drifts

br06.gold_connection: A sudden step in a time series on the day the measuring device changed is a change in the device, not in the thing measured; revert the device to check.
br06.gold_implication: Wear the old ring for three nights and compare the deep-sleep numbers to the new ring's three nights.
br06.hidden_mechanism: a step change that coincides with an instrument change is the instrument, not the world

br07.gold_connection: A lift or a score measured on the same week or the same items the system was tuned against overstates the effect; the honest number comes from data that arrived afterwards.
br07.gold_implication: Recompute the landing page lift on the week after tuning stopped and recompute the eval score on tickets from the following month.
br07.hidden_mechanism: a number measured on the same data it was tuned against is inflated; measure on later data

br09.gold_connection: Identifiers that run in sequence across supposedly independent parties expose a single operator, whether the identifiers are company registration numbers on two proposals or phone numbers across three accounts.
br09.gold_implication: Run an adjacency check on registration numbers across this call's applicants and on phone numbers across new signups, and list any run of three or more consecutive values.
br09.hidden_mechanism: consecutive identifiers across entities that claim to be independent expose one operator

br11.gold_connection: Improvement measured after picking the worst cases is partly reversion to the average, whether the cases are the twenty lowest-scoring eval items or the week with the highest resting heart rate of the year.
br11.gold_implication: Re-run the untouched items alongside the tuned ones, and compare the heart-rate change against a start date chosen at random rather than the worst week.
br11.hidden_mechanism: improvement after selecting the worst cases is partly reversion to the average

br13.gold_connection: Both cash squeezes come from receipt lag against expense cadence, not from profitability: marketplace payouts land 14 days after sales while ad spend bills daily, and the grant pays most of its money months after the costs are incurred.
br13.gold_implication: Build a week-by-week cash model that places each inflow at its actual receipt date and see which weeks go negative under both schedules.
br13.hidden_mechanism: cash gaps come from the lag between doing the work and receiving payment, not from margin

br14.gold_connection: Nothing watches for things that should have happened and did not: a partner deliverable six weeks late and a sensor that went silent both went unnoticed because only submitted items and only error messages are tracked.
br14.gold_implication: Add a weekly check that lists every deliverable and every sensor with no event since its expected date and sends that list even when it is empty.
br14.hidden_mechanism: the absence of an expected event is never alerted, only errors are

br17.gold_connection: Churn at the third billing cycle and dropout around day twenty are the same point: the effort has been paid and the visible result has not arrived yet, so people leave right before they would have seen it.
br17.gold_implication: Send a "what to expect by week three" message on day ten to the next subscriber cohort and compare cycle-three cancellations with the previous cohort.
br17.hidden_mechanism: people quit at the point where effort has been paid but results have not yet appeared

br19.gold_connection: An LLM judge ages like a sensor: even with the snapshot pinned, the same fifty outputs score differently three months apart, so it needs what the sensors get, a fixed reference checked on a schedule with an alarm on divergence.
br19.gold_implication: Re-score the same fifty reference outputs every week and alert when the mean moves more than two percent.
br19.hidden_mechanism: a measuring instrument drifts slowly and silently; a fixed reference re-checked on a schedule catches it

br20.gold_connection: A check that runs less often than the failure lasts never observes it: the nightly eval cannot see twenty-minute mid-day outages, and a ten-minute sensor cannot see two-minute pressure spikes.
br20.gold_implication: Run a small eval every fifteen minutes for a week and compare what it catches against the nightly run.
br20.hidden_mechanism: a check that runs less often than the failures last will never see them

br21.gold_connection: Both funnels spend the expensive step on people a five-question check would have excluded: weeks of proposal writing before an eligibility rejection, and a purchase before a contraindication questionnaire.
br21.gold_implication: Put a five-question eligibility check in front of the grant intake form and count how many applicants it turns away in the first month.
br21.hidden_mechanism: a cheap disqualifying check placed after the expensive step wastes the expensive step

br22.gold_connection: Reporting frequency predicts non-compliance: partners on monthly timesheets are late most months while the quarterly partner is never late, and logging every meal lasted nine days while one weekly weigh-in has lasted five months.
br22.gold_implication: Switch the two monthly partners to quarterly submissions with a one-line monthly confirmation and compare on-time rates over the next two quarters.
br22.hidden_mechanism: the more often reporting is required, the less of it gets done

br23.gold_connection: Both systems accept messages whose timestamp is nowhere near the current time: a sensor with a reset clock corrupted the daily rollup with 2024 readings, and callers reuse a signed ticket days after it was issued; both need a freshness window.
br23.gold_implication: Reject any signed call ticket older than five minutes and any sensor packet whose timestamp is more than ten minutes from server time, then count rejections for a week.
br23.hidden_mechanism: accepting a message whose timestamp is far from now lets stale or replayed messages corrupt the system
